Publish from 3ds Max#

**Status: 4.0.0-beta.1 — upload core tested, needs a real 3ds Max install.** The pymxs script imports cleanly outside Max and its shared Python helper published GLB, OBJ (with units), IFC and FBX (the fallback this plug-in uses), one-shot and resumable, to a real local Verse server; every scene finished and opened; a dead server and a cancel each gave one plain sentence (web/test/fix-verify-aec.mjs). The MAXScript macros cannot be syntax-checked outside Max, and nothing has **been run inside 3ds Max** yet.

Publish to Verse as a toolbar button or quad-menu entry: the scene — or the selection — is exported with 3ds Max's own glTF exporter (Physical / Standard materials → PBR, system units → metres, Z-up → Y-up, textures embedded), uploaded with progress, and the share link is copied and opened. If the glTF exporter is not installed, it falls back to **FBX with embedded media** and the server converts it.

You need: 3ds Max 2023 or newer (Python 3 + pymxs; the glTF exporter ships with 2023+). Windows.

1. Install#

Download VersePublish-3dsMax-4.0.0-beta.1.zip from the downloads page once the packages are published, or build it:

Code
sh integrations/aec/3dsmax/make_package.sh   # -> integrations/aec/3dsmax/dist/VersePublish-3dsMax-4.0.0-beta.1.zip

Unzip somewhere stable and keep the files together (verse_publish_max.py, verse_upload.py, verse_settings.py, VersePublish.ms). Then Scripting ▸ Run Script… ▸ VersePublish.ms — it registers three macros in category Verse (Publish to Verse, Publish selection to Verse, Verse settings). Drag them onto a toolbar from **Customize ▸ Customize User Interface ▸ Toolbars**, or copy VersePublish.ms into <3ds Max>\scripts\startup\ to have them at every start (it finds the Python files next to the original).

2. Server and key#

The Verse settings macro asks for server URL (default https://verse.ctruh.com), API key, account token (from Studio) and bake lighting (blank / preview / final) at the MAXScript prompt.

Nothing is compiled in. They are stored in the per-user file every Verse plug-in shares, %APPDATA%\Ctruh\VersePublish\settings.json, in its 3dsmax section; a server and key saved as shared from another tool apply unless Max sets its own. VERSE_SERVER, VERSE_API_KEY, VERSE_TOKEN override the file. A 4.0.0-beta.1 ~/.verse-publish.json is imported once.

3. Publish#

  1. Run Publish to Verse (or Publish selection to Verse).
  2. Max's progress bar shows exporting → uploading % → building; stages are logged in the MAXScript Listener. The progress bar's Cancel stops it and tells you whether anything was published.
  3. Published! — the link is on the clipboard and opens in the browser.

Success looks like: Published! with the link (also on the clipboard, and opened in the browser); the scene opens in metres whatever the system unit.

Files over 100 MB use the resumable upload: a dropped connection continues where the server got to. When the bundled verse-prepare is present, GLB exports are prepared first.

What gets exported#

  • glTF road (2023+): exportFile … .glb with the glTF exporter — PBR materials, metres, Y-up, textures embedded.
  • FBX fallback: FBX with embedded media and ConvertUnit m; the server converts it (convert.kind: fbx, units from the FBX header) — Upload FBX and OBJ.
  • V-Ray / Corona materials are not translated by the glTF exporter; convert them to Physical materials first for the best match.

Troubleshooting#

Every problem ends in one sentence; the first words tell you which row applies.

You seeWhat it meansDo this
"Could not reach the Verse server at …"Wrong server URL, no internet, or a firewall / proxy blocking the plug-in.Check Server URL in Verse settings (the Verse macro) (default https://verse.ctruh.com) and open it in a browser.
"The Verse server at … did not recognise the account token …"The token is mistyped, was revoked, or belongs to another server. Nothing was uploaded.Copy the token again from Studio, or clear it to publish without an account.
"The server did not accept your API key or account token …"This server only takes uploads with an API key; the sentence ends with its reason.Enter the key from the server's operator in Verse settings (the Verse macro).
"Upload limit reached: …"The hourly upload limit, or the API key's daily quota.Wait as the sentence says, or add an account token from Studio (a higher limit).
"The server is busy right now. …" / "The server is out of storage. …"The server's build queue or disk is full. Your file is fine.Publish again in a few minutes.
"The upload kept failing …"The connection dropped again and again.Publish again when the connection is steady; a large upload continues where it stopped.
"Verse cannot build … files yet. Export the model as GLB (or FBX / OBJ) and publish that file instead."STEP / IGES / native CAD files are not built by the server yet.Export GLB (or FBX / OBJ) and publish that.
"Stopped waiting for the server. The scene is still being built …"You cancelled after the upload; the server keeps building.The scene appears in your Verse dashboard (with an account token) when it is ready.
No Verse category in Customize ▸ ToolbarsVersePublish.ms was not run (or was moved).Scripting ▸ Run Script ▸ VersePublish.ms from the unzipped folder, then customise again.
"The scene is empty — there is nothing to publish."No visible objects.Unhide the scene, then publish again.

Anything else: send the whole sentence (and, for a build error, the scene name) to hello@ctruh.com.
